jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Enterprise Architecture based in Canada.

As Director, Enterprise Architecture, you will shape the organization's long-term technology vision and lead the evolution of its enterprise architecture practice. You will provide strategic and people leadership to a multidisciplinary team of architects, ensuring technology investments support business priorities and deliver sustainable value. Working closely with senior business and technology leaders, you will translate organizational strategy into scalable technology roadmaps and architectural solutions. You will oversee architecture governance, standards, and practices while guiding major transformation initiatives. With a strong focus on innovation, security, resilience, and responsible AI adoption, you will help build a future-ready technology ecosystem. This hybrid leadership opportunity combines strategic influence, technical expertise, and team development.

Accountabilities

You will lead the enterprise architecture function, establish architectural direction, and ensure technology decisions support long-term organizational objectives. By collaborating with business and technology stakeholders, you will drive transformation, strengthen governance, and develop a high-performing architecture team.

Lead, coach, and develop a team of architects, establishing clear expectations, performance objectives, career development opportunities, and technical growth priorities.
Define and communicate architectural strategies for major business and technology initiatives, ensuring alignment with enterprise objectives and the long-term technology vision.
Establish and maintain architecture principles, standards, patterns, guidelines, and governance frameworks to promote consistency and effective decision-making.
Partner with senior business and technology leaders to understand strategic priorities and translate business requirements into technology strategies, roadmaps, and architectural outcomes.
Coordinate solution, data, security, infrastructure, and enterprise architecture disciplines to ensure consistency across the technology ecosystem.
Guide product owners, engineering leaders, architects, designers, and developers in key architectural decisions, including buy-versus-build assessments, cloud adoption, integration patterns, and real-time versus batch processing.
Oversee the design and implementation of solutions across business applications and technology platforms, ensuring compliance with enterprise architecture, security, and business requirements.
Provide architectural leadership for major transformation programs and complex technology initiatives, identifying dependencies, risks, opportunities, and cross-functional considerations.
Assess the existing technology portfolio and develop roadmaps to address technical debt, aging systems, regulatory requirements, architectural gaps, and evolving business needs.
Evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, automation, cloud platforms, modern engineering practices, fintech developments, and vendor solutions.
Promote responsible technology adoption by assessing how emerging capabilities can support new business models, improve operations, and deliver long-term value.

Requirements

The ideal candidate is an experienced technology leader with a strong background in enterprise architecture, strategic planning, and organizational transformation. You should combine broad technical expertise with proven people leadership skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders in complex environments.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of progressive technology experience, including substantial experience in solution architecture and enterprise architecture, preferably within banking or financial services.
Demonstrated experience leading, managing, coaching, and developing architecture teams or senior technology professionals, with responsibility for performance and capability development.
Current expertise in artificial intelligence, including AI-enabled architecture, AI governance, and AI specification-driven development.
Broad knowledge of software architecture, application development, data management, cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud computing, automation, and modern engineering practices.
Experience establishing, developing, or maturing an enterprise architecture practice, including governance models, architectural standards, principles, roadmaps, and decision-making frameworks.
Proven ability to influence senior executives and business leaders and translate business strategies into practical technology strategies and architectural direction.
Strong experience with cloud architecture, preferably Microsoft Azure.
In-depth understanding of integration patterns, APIs, microservices, event-driven architectures, and modern application architecture.
Excellent people leadership and communication skills, with the ability to build strong teams, establish accountability, and develop technical talent.
Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, including the ability to navigate ambiguity, balance competing priorities, and drive alignment.
Ability to connect business objectives, customer outcomes, organizational capabilities, risk considerations, and technology investments.

Additional Qualifications That Would Be Considered An Asset Include

Experience with modern core banking platforms and a strong understanding of the banking and fintech technology landscape.
Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks and methodologies such as TOGAF, with the ability to apply them pragmatically.
Knowledge of Agile methodologies and modern product and software development practices.
Experience working closely with product management and engineering leadership teams.
A collaborative and adaptable leadership approach, with the ability to guide teams through organizational change and technological transformation.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary: CAD 180,000–200,000, depending on qualifications, skills, experience, and internal equity.
Annual incentive program: Eligibility for additional performance-based compensation, subject to program requirements.
Customizable benefits: Flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet individual and family needs.
Generous paid vacation: 3–4 weeks of vacation annually for new employees, with additional days earned over time.
Additional holidays: Two extra days off beyond British Columbia's 11 statutory holidays.
Care days: Additional time off to support personal or family illness.
Immediate health coverage: Medical and dental benefits starting on the first day of employment, with three coverage levels available.
Defined benefit pension plan: Retirement benefits providing a guaranteed income for life.
Hybrid working arrangements: Flexibility to work primarily from a home office in the Lower Mainland or Toronto, with Vancouver-based employees potentially expected to attend the office at least once per week.
Professional development: Opportunities to strengthen leadership capabilities, develop technical expertise, and pursue long-term career growth.
Inclusive workplace culture: A collaborative environment that values diversity, accessibility, social responsibility, and individual perspectives.
Purpose-driven work: The opportunity to contribute to initiatives focused on financial inclusion, social impact, community resilience, and sustainable development.

In this strategic leadership role, you will drive the development and delivery of HR technology solutions that support organizational priorities and workforce management across a large, complex organization. You will oversee the implementation and ongoing optimization of the Workday HCM platform, ensuring systems are reliable, scalable, and aligned with evolving business needs. Leading a dedicated HR Technology team, you will establish the governance structures, operational frameworks, and service capabilities required for long-term success. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to interpret data, identify trends, assess business requirements, and develop effective solutions.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence decisions and build relationships at all organizational levels.
Proven leadership experience managing, mentoring, and developing technical teams while promoting collaboration, accountability, and high performance.
In-depth understanding of HR technology, human capital management principles, organizational change management, and business process optimization.

jobs.title: Head of Customer Support
jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our customers are developers and technical teams running production workloads through our API. When something goes wrong, such as a failed request, a surprising bill or a confusing savings number, they need fast, accurate, technically credible help. Support is part of the product.

The role You'll build and lead customer support at Cheaper Inference from the ground up. You'll handle tickets yourself at first, then design the systems, tools, documentation and team that let support grow with the company. You'll be accountable for how fast we respond, how well we resolve issues, how satisfied customers are and how much of what you learn gets back to the product team.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. A large share of our support is technical. You'll often be the first to spot an API issue, a billing edge case or a confusing part of the dashboard.

What you'll do Own the support function.
Set up support channels (email, in-app chat, Discord or Slack communities), choose and configure the tools, and define SLAs, priority levels and escalation paths.
Handle tickets directly at first.
Answer technical questions about API integration, streaming, rate limits, errors, model availability, request headers, prompt A/B experiments and billing.
Run incident communication.
Work with engineering during outages or slowdowns. Post updates on the status page, let affected customers know proactively and follow up after incidents.
Build self-serve help.
Create and maintain help center articles, troubleshooting guides, FAQs and macros so customers can solve common problems themselves. Work with the docs team to fill gaps.
Handle billing and account issues.
Resolve questions about usage, invoices, credits, refunds, savings attribution and plan changes accurately and fairly.
Get customer feedback to the product team.
Tag and analyze tickets to find recurring problems, bugs and feature requests. Report clear, prioritized findings to product and engineering.
Use automation wisely.
Set up AI-assisted support (triage, suggested replies, a documentation chatbot) where it helps, without letting quality slip.
Hire and grow the team.
Decide when and who to hire, including support engineers and specialists. Build the onboarding, training and quality review processes they'll need.
Measure everything.
Track first response time, time to resolution, CSAT, ticket volume per customer and the share of issues customers solve on their own. Report on these regularly and keep improving them.
Support key accounts.
Work with sales and success on onboarding, migrations and dedicated support for high-value customers.

What success looks like First 90 days:
Support tools, SLAs and escalation paths in place. A core help center live. Response times and CSAT measured and improving. A regular report of customer feedback going to product.
First year:
A support operation that can grow, with a strong self-serve rate, consistently high CSAT, a clear plan for hiring the team and measurable product improvements driven by support findings.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in customer support or support engineering, including at least 1–2 years leading support or building it from scratch, ideally at an API, developer tool, infrastructure or SaaS company.
Strong technical skills. You're comfortable reading API docs, testing requests with curl or Postman, reading logs and error codes, and talking with engineers in their terms.
Experience with support platforms (e.g., Zendesk, Intercom, Plain, Front, Help Scout) and status page tools.
Excellent writing. Your replies are clear, empathetic and accurate, and your documentation actually gets used.
Experience handling billing and usage-based pricing questions.
Calm judgment during incidents and escalations.
A data-driven approach to support metrics and process improvement.
An owner's mindset and comfort doing the work yourself at an early-stage company.

Nice to have Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic or similar) or AI infrastructure products.
Basic scripting or SQL to investigate issues without waiting for engineering.
Experience running developer communities on Discord or Slack.
Experience setting up AI-assisted support workflows.

Why join Compensation: $100,000 - $135,000 + equity
You'll build a core function from scratch and shape how customers experience Cheaper Inference.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering, where your input directly shapes the product.
You'll join a small, high-leverage team with real ownership.

jobs.title: Head of Supply Partnerships (Inference Providers)
jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We help our customers save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our supply of inference capacity limits how far we can grow. The more good, reliable, low-cost capacity we have, the bigger the discount, the more models we can offer and the more customers we can serve.

The role You'll be the first person focused full-time on the supply side of the business. You'll find, sign, onboard and manage our relationships with inference providers. These include GPU clouds, model labs, resellers, enterprises with reserved capacity they don't use and neoclouds. You'll be accountable for how much capacity we have, what it costs, how reliable it is and how many models it covers.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. In this job, commercial deals and technical details go together: a good deal on a slow or unreliable endpoint is a bad deal.

What you'll do Build the supplier pipeline.
Find and rank providers with surplus or discountable capacity across models, regions and hardware. Run outreach from first contact to a live integration.
Negotiate and close.
Set pricing, volume commitments, rate limits, SLAs, payment terms and data-handling terms. Structure deals that keep us below list price while staying fair and sustainable for providers.
Onboard providers.
Work with engineering to connect new providers to our routing layer. Meet latency and throughput targets and report accurate usage.
Manage live relationships.
Track each provider's uptime, latency, error rates, fill rates and how competitive their prices are. Run regular business reviews, handle escalations and expand the relationships that work.
Protect supply resilience.
Avoid relying too heavily on one provider, keep backup capacity for our most popular models and plan ahead for demand spikes and new model launches.
Track the market.
Follow GPU and token pricing, new model releases, provider roadmaps and competitors. Turn what you learn into a supply strategy and pricing recommendations.
Own trust and compliance with partners.
Make sure providers meet our standards for data retention, privacy, security (e.g., SOC 2) and acceptable use. Work with legal on contracts and DPAs.
Shape the marketplace.
Help design incentives, pricing mechanics and provider-facing tools and processes that attract and keep good capacity.

What success looks like First 90 days:
A mapped list of target providers, at least 3–5 new providers signed and live, and a clear view of the health of current supply.
First year:
A deep, diverse provider base covering all major models, measurable gains in price and reliability, and a repeatable process for bringing on new providers.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in partnerships, business development, supply or procurement, ideally at an AI infrastructure company, cloud or GPU provider, or a two-sided marketplace.
An existing network across inference providers, GPU clouds or model labs, or a clear plan for building one fast.
A strong commercial sense. You're comfortable with unit economics, margin, usage-based pricing and capacity commitments.
Enough technical depth to discuss tokens per second, time to first token, rate limits, quantization, context windows and API compatibility with engineers on both sides.
A track record of negotiating and closing complex contracts.
Comfort with data. You can build the dashboards and models you need to manage supply (SQL or spreadsheets).
An owner's mindset and comfort with ambiguity at an early-stage company.

Nice to have Experience with open-weight model serving (vLLM, TGI, SGLang) or GPU capacity markets.
A background in marketplace design, trading or commodity procurement.
Familiarity with enterprise security and compliance reviews.

Why join Compensation: $150,000 - $250,000 + equity
You'll own a function that directly sets our product's price, quality and growth.
You'll work at the center of a fast-moving market for AI compute.
You'll join a small, high-leverage team with real ownership.
